scope: Full Power Stack daily refresh: US, Hong Kong/China and Malaysia; all established categories and current holdings reviewed. GPACKET excluded as instructed.
headlineRead: Hormuz/tanker risk remains the dominant immediate macro shock, but today's important second-order development is demand destruction and rerouting: Brent rose to about $96.80 and WTI $92.14 while Hormuz commodity traffic fell to roughly 10 ships/day, the lowest since May; China's August seaborne crude imports remained about 40% below pre-conflict levels. At the same time, high US real/nominal yields and weak-end credit stress keep valuation discipline critical. AI physical demand remains unusually resilient, with Foxconn reporting record August revenue and stronger Q3 visibility on AI demand.
whatsNewNow: Brent ~$96.80 and WTI ~$92.14 as direct tanker attacks keep Hormuz risk elevated; OPEC+ kept October output policy unchanged.
Hormuz commodity traffic averaged about 10 ships/day over the latest 10-day window, lowest since May; no VLCC exited after Wednesday in the cited Kpler window.
China seaborne crude imports rose modestly MoM in August but remained ~40% below pre-war levels, confirming material demand/routing adaptation rather than unlimited price elasticity.
US weak-end credit stress is becoming a first-class valuation filter: CCC-and-lower spreads were reported around 10.53 percentage points, up from 8.08 a year ago, with default actions rising in 2026.
Foxconn's August revenue reached a record T$921.8bn (+51.98% YoY) and management expects Q3 to outperform market expectations on AI demand, independently confirming real AI server demand.
Japan's record August FX intervention and near-fully-priced September BOJ hike add a global-yields/FX dimension to the restrictive funding regime.
Sigma Lithium's sole operating mine was halted by a Brazilian court. This is a real supply disruption, but not enough to overturn the broader lithium oversupply/dilution discipline.
whatMattersMostNow: Hormuz/refined-product/shipping risk versus visible demand destruction and rerouting
Restrictive US real yields + rising weak-end credit stress
AI power/grid/time-to-power capex with funded-load quality screens
Copper structural demand versus distorted/high visible inventories
Energy-security rerouting toward non-Hormuz crude and Atlantic LNG
Selective profitable AI software/automation rather than blanket duration
Gold/fiscal hedge versus real-yield and USD headwinds
Lithium supply interruptions versus still-demanding oversupply economics

developingThemes.name: Hormuz / Refined Products / Direct Tanker Risk
developingThemes.whyNow: Direct attacks on oil transport continue; Brent ~$96.80, WTI ~$92.14 and Hormuz traffic is at the lowest since May.
developingThemes.marketTransmission: Crude, diesel/gasoline, freight, inflation expectations, yields, consumer purchasing power, Asian crude availability and tanker economics.
developingThemes.confirmation: Further traffic decline, sustained product cracks, inventory draws or additional tanker attacks.
developingThemes.invalidation: Durable ceasefire plus normalised shipping and collapsing product spreads.
developingThemes.nextTest: Hormuz traffic, EIA inventories/products, CPI/PPI and Asian refinery runs.
developingThemes.action: Hold quality integrated/refining exposure; do not chase geopolitical gaps.

developingThemes.name: Higher-for-Longer + Weak-End Credit Stress
developingThemes.whyNow: 10Y remained near 4.79% at the last cash close, real 10Y near 2.45%, while reported CCC-and-lower spreads reached ~10.53 percentage points.
developingThemes.marketTransmission: Raises hurdle rates for leveraged power/data-centre projects, long-duration software/robotics, housing and weak balance sheets while rewarding current cash flow.
developingThemes.confirmation: CPI/PPI hot, 10Y/30Y retest highs, CCC stress widens further.
developingThemes.invalidation: Clear disinflation plus sustained yield and weak-credit spread compression.
developingThemes.nextTest: PPI Sep 10, CPI Sep 11, Treasury curve and HY/CCC spreads.
developingThemes.action: Keep valuation/FCF discipline; avoid financing-dependent stories.

developingThemes.name: AI Power / Grid / Time-to-Power + Funded Demand
developingThemes.whyNow: Foxconn's record August revenue and improved Q3 outlook confirm AI server demand while Vertiv's UIG deal reinforces microgrids/onsite power as a deployment bottleneck solution.
developingThemes.marketTransmission: Supports electrical equipment, transmission, cooling, onsite generation and automation; capital competition raises financing costs and punishes ghost-load pipelines.
developingThemes.confirmation: Named customer backlog, deposits, order growth and FCF conversion.
developingThemes.invalidation: Cancellations, falling utilisation or unfunded load queues overwhelming booked demand.
developingThemes.nextTest: Supplier order updates, hyperscaler capex, YTL contracted utilisation and backlog conversion.
developingThemes.action: Prefer funded backlog and cash conversion over requested MW.

developingThemes.name: Energy Security Rerouting + Asian Demand Destruction
developingThemes.whyNow: China's seaborne crude imports remain roughly 40% below pre-conflict levels while buyers seek Russian, Americas and alternative-route barrels; Iraq is also pursuing non-Hormuz capacity.
developingThemes.marketTransmission: Caps one-way crude upside, increases route miles/storage/logistics value and supports US/Atlantic LNG and non-Gulf crude exporters.
developingThemes.confirmation: Persistent Asian import substitution, higher Atlantic exports and new pipeline/terminal commitments.
developingThemes.invalidation: Rapid Hormuz normalisation and return of Middle East flows.
developingThemes.nextTest: China/India import mix, Iraq exports, US LNG utilisation and tanker rates.
developingThemes.action: Favor infrastructure/logistics and contracted LNG over pure price beta.

developingThemes.name: Copper: Grid Demand vs Inventory Distortion
developingThemes.whyNow: Grid/electrification demand remains structural, but visible global inventories are elevated and geography/tariff stockpiling complicates the scarcity signal.
developingThemes.marketTransmission: Benefits low-cost producers over time but raises equipment/input costs; near-term copper beta needs inventory confirmation.
developingThemes.confirmation: Ex-US inventory draw plus stronger physical premiums/order demand.
developingThemes.invalidation: Sustained inventory builds and weak Chinese/industrial demand.
developingThemes.nextTest: LME/COMEX/SHFE stocks, China demand and FCX operating recovery.
developingThemes.action: FCX remains pullback-first; do not treat high inventories as a clean shortage signal.

developingThemes.name: Food / Grain / Fertilizer Affordability
developingThemes.whyNow: High fuel/freight and disrupted fertilizer/feedstock flows keep farm economics under pressure; demand elasticity differs sharply by input.
developingThemes.marketTransmission: Nitrogen/premium genetics are harder to defer; potash/phosphate, crop protection, irrigation and machinery face greater deferral risk.
developingThemes.confirmation: Healthy crop/input ratios, application rates and producer margins.
developingThemes.invalidation: Farm margins collapse enough to force broad application/capex cuts.
developingThemes.nextTest: Crop/input ratios, fertilizer flows, grain exports and application guidance.
developingThemes.action: Prefer CF/CTVA/BG quality; AGCO remains second-stage recovery.

developingThemes.name: Uranium / Nuclear Fuel-Cycle Scarcity
developingThemes.whyNow: Western nuclear buildout remains intact while advanced-reactor fuel availability, including HALEU/plutonium pathways, is a real bottleneck.
developingThemes.marketTransmission: Supports incumbent fuel/conversion and proven nuclear suppliers more than pre-revenue reactor concepts.
developingThemes.confirmation: Long-term contracting, conversion/enrichment pricing and funded deployments.
developingThemes.invalidation: Contracting stalls or supply expands faster than reactor/fuel demand.
developingThemes.action: CCJ remains preferred uranium quality exposure near disciplined entry levels.

developingThemes.name: Selective AI Software / Cyber / Physical Automation
developingThemes.whyNow: AI monetisation is visible in selected software and physical-operations platforms, but high real yields punish weak FCF and narrative-only names.
developingThemes.marketTransmission: Rewards ARR/RPO/FCF and real deployment ROI; compresses speculative multiples.
developingThemes.confirmation: Durable growth with expanding FCF and customer economics.
developingThemes.invalidation: Decelerating bookings/retention or valuation re-expansion without cash conversion.
developingThemes.action: Pullback-only; robotics sequence remains fixed/warehouse > cobots/mobile > humanoids.

developingThemes.name: Gold / Fiscal-Monetary Hedge
developingThemes.whyNow: Geopolitics and fiscal concerns support the structural hedge, but real yields near 2.45% and Fed-hike risk remain tactical headwinds.
developingThemes.marketTransmission: Gold benefits from fiscal/sovereign distrust but competes directly with high real yields and USD strength.
developingThemes.confirmation: Gold holds/rises despite high real yields or yields begin falling.
developingThemes.invalidation: Persistent real-yield/USD rise with bullion breakdown.
developingThemes.nextTest: US CPI/PPI, real yields and central-bank/ETF flows.

developingThemes.name: Lithium Supply Interruptions vs ESS Demand
developingThemes.whyNow: Sigma Lithium's only operating mine was halted by a Brazilian court, creating a real supply interruption, while grid-scale storage demand remains strong.
developingThemes.marketTransmission: Can tighten individual supply chains, but broad miner economics still depend on oversupply, dilution and project discipline.
developingThemes.confirmation: Multiple supply curtailments plus sustained battery/ESS demand tighten balances.
developingThemes.invalidation: Rapid mine restart or continued inventory/price weakness despite outages.
developingThemes.nextTest: Sigma legal process, lithium prices, producer curtailments and ESS deployments.
developingThemes.action: Research only; do not promote speculative miners on one outage.
